question: What happens to the baby's skull bones during moulding in labour?

options.B: They separate and increase in width
options.D: They overlap to reduce head size

explanation: Great job! As the baby passes through the birth canal, the skull bones gently overlap at the sutures to make the head a bit smaller and help delivery go smoothly. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h1)

question: Why are the sutures and fontanelles so important during a vaginal delivery?

options.A: They allow the brain to expand rapidly during birth
options.B: They provide a cushion of fluid against uterine pressure
options.C: They permit the skull bones to shift and overlap safely
options.D: They supply extra oxygenated blood to the fetal scalp

explanation: You've got this! Those flexible spaces between the baby's skull bones act like natural shock absorbers, letting the head adapt to the birth canal without hurting the brain. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h1)

question: What is the main difference between normal (physiological) and abnormal (pathological) moulding?

options.A: Physiological moulding is normal and reversible, while pathological moulding involves excessive, damaging forces
options.B: Physiological moulding only happens in premature babies, whereas pathological moulding happens at term
options.C: Pathological moulding causes soft swelling while physiological moulding causes hard ridges
options.D: Pathological moulding involves bone fractures and permanent shape changes

explanation: Spot on! Normal moulding happens in almost every birth and goes away on its own. Pathological moulding comes from extreme, harsh pressure that can cause harm. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h2)

question: A newborn has rigid, tightly locked overlapping skull bones after a very long, difficult labour. What do we call this?
explanation: Well done. When the bones are jammed together tightly from a difficult, prolonged labour, it's considered pathological moulding and needs close attention. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h2)

question: Which newborn scalp swelling is known for crossing right across the cranial suture lines?
explanation: Correct! Caput is just fluid under the scalp skin, so it easily crosses over the suture lines. Think of it like a soft, spongy cushion. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h3)

question: Why must a baby with a large cephalhematoma be watched closely for jaundice?

options.A: The liver gets compressed by the outer swelling and stops working
options.B: The baby stops feeding due to pain from the blood pocket
options.C: Infection in the hematoma spreads quickly to the liver
options.D: The trapped blood cells break down and release excess bilirubin

explanation: You're doing great! As the body reabsorbs that pooled blood under the scalp, it releases bilirubin into the baby's system, which can turn their skin yellow (jaundice). [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h3)

question: What usually causes bleeding inside the skull during severe fetal moulding?

options.A: High blood pressure caused by maternal pushing
options.B: Lack of vitamin K in the newborn circulation
options.C: Stretching and tearing of bridging veins inside the skull
options.D: Rupture of scalp arteries from vacuum suction

explanation: Spot on. When the skull bones overlap too severely, they stretch and strain the tiny veins inside, causing them to tear and bleed. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h4)

question: A newborn delivered after a tough, instrument-assisted birth is very sleepy (lethargic) and has a high-pitched cry. What should the nurse suspect?
explanation: You nailed it. Unusual sleepiness and a high-pitched cry are classic red flags that there might be pressure or bleeding inside the baby's head. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h4)

question: What is the right nursing action when you spot rigid, overlapping skull bones on a newborn?

options.A: Document the finding and monitor without forcing the bones apart
options.B: Apply warm compresses to soften the cranial sutures
options.C: Gently massage the bones back into a normal round shape
options.D: Wrap the head tightly with a bandage to keep bones in place

explanation: Brilliant! Never try to push or massage overlapping bones back into place—that can cause more injury. Just document what you see and keep a close eye on the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h5)

question: Which assessment is essential when checking a newborn's skull after a difficult birth with heavy moulding?

options.A: Checking deep tendon reflexes in the lower extremities only
options.B: Performing a lumbar puncture immediately on all babies
options.C: Measuring head circumference and assessing fontanelle texture
options.D: Aspirating fluid from the suture lines with a small needle

explanation: Correct! Checking the head size and feeling whether the fontanelles are soft, flat, or bulging helps you catch any hidden swelling early. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h5)

question: What specific details should a nurse include when charting newborn skull moulding?

options.A: The mother's exact pelvis shape and measurements
options.B: The degree of bone overlapping and presence of scalp lesions
options.C: The exact volume of blood lost by the mother
options.D: The specific brand of instruments used during delivery

explanation: You've got this! Good nursing notes focus on the baby's actual condition—how the bones are aligned and if there is any swelling or scratches on the scalp. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h6)

question: A newborn with severe moulding and a large cephalhematoma is in the nursery. Which nursing action is WRONG and unsafe?

options.A: Observing the skin closely for developing yellow discoloration
options.B: Encouraging gentle feeding and assessing for sucking strength
options.C: Monitoring vital signs and neurological status frequently
options.D: Attempting to massage the pooled blood away from the skull bone

explanation: Spot on! Massaging a cephalhematoma or moulded skull is dangerous because it can cause more bleeding and tissue damage. Hands off the swelling! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h6)
